content.heading:
A century of stories meets
a new hospitality
content.paragraph: Behind this mannered Italian Renaissance facade is a century of glamorous mischief. Today, it’s an icon with open arms, a high-spirited destination that welcomes you to the heart of contemporary San Diego.

content.heading:
First sips, small bites
& big nights out.
content.paragraph: For visitors and locals, Guild dining is a journey, an invitation to to savor our worlds. The Lobby Bar knows its classics from its off-menu surprises. California’s first Zuma serves up the sushi and robata that have made it an international standard-setter from London to Miami, Vail to Abu Dhabi. Poolside, there’s always fresh, easy West Coast goodness, and the Mediterranean influences daytime offerings in The Courtyard.

content.heading:
A room
for every stay
content.paragraph: From intimate rooms to expansive loft suites, each space brings together The Guild’s historic character, thoughtful design and modern comfort.

The best of
San Diego is right here
content.paragraph: The San Diego on our doorstep includes the city’s favorite neighborhoods and attractions – and best of all, you can walk to them. From the harbor and Seaport Village to the Museum of Contemporary Art, Little Italy and the Gaslamp, the past, future and excitement of the city are yours to discover.

openQuestions: The three decoration SVGs (building illustration, postmark stamp, back arrow) have no Webflow asset id (figma/assets.json webflowAssetId is null). Upload them with the asset pipeline before the Designer session, or embed them inline?

happenings-indiv/02 and blog-indiv/02 (identical, both CMS templates) are excluded from this family: left-aligned caps title, long paragraph and a burgundy octagon CTA that overlaps the paragraph in Figma. Decided as a unique item per the orchestrator rule. The orchestrator should add an entry for them (suggested class family text-intro-cta, reusing text-style-eyebrow-caps and the global button), or fold them into the CMS template entry.

arts/02 sets its script heading in accent green (#29310C); the other script headings are #000000. The plan uses color-neutral-900 for all of them. Keep arts green with an is-accent heading modifier, or treat it as a design inconsistency?
rooms-individual/02 back link: should it point to /rooms (rooms-collection) on every room page? The page is the rooms CMS template.
No mobile or tablet design exists. The plan scales the script heading 5 / 4 / 3.25 / 2.75rem and the section padding 14 / 10 / 6 / 5rem. Confirm.
deviations: is-tall is kept as the brief asks, but the 700px versus 600px height difference in Figma is almost all content (the 441x254 building illustration). Its only style delta is 2.5rem more bottom padding (home bottom gap 272px versus about 240px elsewhere). K01 may drop it.

Added element modifiers is-wide (script-intro-centered_text) and is-bottom (script-intro-centered_figure). They are content-layout modifiers inside the one family, not a second component. Paragraph widths in Figma are 588px (36.75rem) and 742 to 744px (46.5rem); the stamp sits below the paragraph while the building sits above the heading.

Script headings are rotated -0.1288 rad (-7.38deg) in figma/raw. The plan rotates script-intro-centered_heading with transform and gives it 3rem top and bottom margin so the rotated glyphs do not collide. Figma's measured heading-to-paragraph gap is about 107px on most instances and 67px on home; the plan uses one gap (2.5rem row gap plus 3rem margin, 88px).
Heading colour #000000 has no variable; the plan uses color-neutral-900 (#262118).

Dropped the cream H4-CAPS text "Contemporary Japanese Dining at The Guild Hotel" found on rooms-collection, guidelines, legal and corporate: it is cream on cream at x 945, invisible in every crop, a leftover layer.
padding-section-xlarge is a new shared utility; the brief's padding-section-* set tops out at 7rem, half the Figma gap.
Removed the trailing spaces from the dining-collection paragraph.
Brief instances happenings-indiv/02 and blog-indiv/02 are not covered by this plan; see excludedInstances and openQuestions.

Preview scale: plan values are Figma px at 1600 converted 1:1 to rem, so at 1440 the preview reads about 10 percent larger than the crop scaled to 1440. Kept 1:1 on purpose; Webflow has no fluid type scale here.
